K.|author-link1=Fan Chung|title=Spectral graph theory|series=CBMS Regional Conference Series in Mathematics|volume=92|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|location=Providence, RI|year=1997|isbn=0-8218-0315-8|zbl=0867.05046|doi=10.1090/cbms/092}}</ref> Later, they introduced a [[Green's function]] as defined for graphs, amounting to a [[pseudo-inverse]] of the [[graph Laplacian]].{{ran|CY00}} Their work is naturally applicable to the study of [[hitting time]]s for [[random walk]]s and related topics.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Clustering and embedding using commute times|last2=Hancock|first2=Edwin R.|last1=Qiu|first1=Huaijun|journal=[[IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence]]|volume=29|issue=11|year=2007|pages=1873–1890|doi=10.1109/TPAMI.2007.1103|pmid=17848771|bibcode=2007ITPAM..29.1873Q |s2cid=1043277|author-link2=Edwin Hancock}}</ref><ref>{{cite conference|last1=Smola|first1=Alexander J.|last2=Kondor|first2=Risi|title=Kernels and regularization on graphs|pages=144–158|book-title=Learning theory and kernel machines|conference=16th annual conference on learning theory and 7th kernel workshop, Washington, DC, USA, August 24–27, 2003|year=2003|editor1-first=Bernhard|editor1-last=Schölkopf|editor2-first=Manfred K.|editor2-last=Warmuth|series=[[Lecture Notes in Computer Science]]|volume=2777|isbn=978-3-540-40720-1|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45167-9_12|zbl=1274.68351|editor-link1=Bernhard Schölkopf|editor-link2=Manfred K. Warmuth|s2cid=7326173}}</ref>

In the interest of finding general graph-theoretic contexts for their results, Chung and Yau introduced a notion of [[Ricci-flat manifold|Ricci-flatness]] of a graph.<ref name="fanchung" /> A more flexible notion of Ricci curvature, dealing with [[Markov chain]]s on [[metric space]]s, was later introduced by Yann Ollivier. Yong Lin, Linyuan Lu, and Yau developed some of the basic theory of Ollivier's definition in the special context of graph theory, considering for instance the Ricci curvature of [[Erdős–Rényi model|Erdős–Rényi random graphs]].{{ran|LLY11}} Lin and Yau also considered the ''curvature–dimension inequalities'' introduced earlier by [[Dominique Bakry]] and Michel Émery, relating it and Ollivier's curvature to Chung–Yau's notion of Ricci-flatness.{{ran|LY10}} They were further able to prove general lower bounds on Bakry–Émery and Ollivier's curvatures in the case of locally finite graphs.<ref>{{cite journal|mr=3164168|last1=Jost|first1=Jürgen|author-link1=Jürgen Jost|last2=Liu|first2=Shiping|title=Ollivier's Ricci curvature, local clustering and curvature–dimension inequalities on graphs|journal=[[Discrete & Computational Geometry]]|volume=51|year=2014|issue=2|pages=300–322|doi=10.1007/s00454-013-9558-1|doi-access=free|zbl=1294.05061|arxiv=1103.4037}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Yau has received honorary professorships from many Chinese universities, including [[Hunan Normal University]], [[Peking University]], [[Nankai University]], and [[Tsinghua University]]. He has honorary degrees from many international universities, including [[Harvard University]], [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]], and [[University of Waterloo]]. He is a foreign member of the National Academies of Sciences of China, India, and Russia.

His awards include:
* 1975–1976, [[Sloan Fellow]].
* 1981, [[Oswald Veblen Prize in Geometry]].
* 1981, [[John J. Carty Award for the Advancement of Science]], [[United States National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_carty |title=John J. Carty Award for the Advancement of Science |publisher=[[United States National Academy of Sciences]] |access-date=Jan 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229180532/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_carty |archive-date=2010-12-29 }}</ref>
* 1982, [[Fields Medal]], for  "his contributions to partial differential equations, to the Calabi conjecture in [[algebraic geometry]], to the positive mass conjecture of general relativity theory, and to real and complex Monge–Ampère equations."
* 1982, elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]
* 1982, [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].
* 1984–1985, [[MacArthur Fellow]].
* 1991, [[Humboldt Research Award]], [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], Germany.
* 1993, elected to the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]]
* 1994, [[Crafoord Prize]].<ref>"...for his development of non-linear techniques in differential geometry leading to the solution of several outstanding problems."</ref>
* 1997, [[United States]] [[National Medal of Science]].
* 2003, China International Scientific and Technological Cooperation Award, for  "his outstanding contribution to PRC in aspects of making progress in sciences and technology, training researchers."
* 2010, [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics]], for "his work in geometric analysis and mathematical physics".<ref>Malkah Fleisher, [http://www.israelnationalnews.com/News/News.aspx/135820 Winners of Prestigious Wolf Prize Announced]</ref>
* 2018, [[International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics#Marcel Grossmann Awards|Marcel Grossmann Awards]], "for the proof of the positivity of total mass in the theory of general relativity and perfecting as well the concept of quasi-local mass, for his proof of the Calabi conjecture, for his continuous inspiring role in the study of black holes physics."<ref>Marcel Grossmann, [http://www.icra.it/mg/awards/Welcome.htm#15th 15th Marcel Grossmann Meeting]</ref>
* 2023, [[Shaw Prize]] in Mathematical Sciences.<ref>[https://www.shawprize.org/news/announcement-press-conference-2023-press-release Shaw Prize 2023]</ref>
